questions.html:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : SVM can handle both linear and non-linear classification.
S2 : Kernel functions map data to higher dimensions for linear separation.
Which following is correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• SVM is a strong classifier that handles linear data by finding a separating hyperplane. For non-linear data, it uses Kernel functions to work with data that cannot be separated in the original space. Thus, SVM manages both linear and nonlinear problems. So, S1 is correct.
• Kernel functions map data implicitly into a higher-dimensional space, making non-linearly separable data separable by a hyperplane. This Kernel trick enables SVM to classify nonlinear data effectively. So, S2 is correct.

questions.html:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : The bias-variance tradeoff refers to the balance between underfitting and overfitting in predictive models.
S2 : High variance models tend to fit the training data very well but perform poorly on unseen data.
Which following is correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• The bias-variance tradeoff refers to balancing underfitting and overfitting in a model. High bias causes underfitting where the model is too simple to capture the data pattern. High variance causes overfitting where the model fits training data too closely but fails on new data. So, S1 is correct.
• High variance models fit the training data very well, resulting in low training error. However, they perform poorly on unseen data because they do not generalize well, leading to overfitting. So, S2 is correct.

Consider the following statements about Decision Trees:
S1 : A fully grown decision tree has low bias and high variance.
S2 : Pruning a decision tree is a technique to reduce variance at the cost of increasing bias.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• A fully grown tree perfectly fits training data (overfitting), so low bias, but it’s sensitive to small changes → high variance. So, S1 is correct.
• Pruning simplifies the tree → less overfitting (reduces variance), but may not capture all patterns (increases bias). So, S2 is correct.

Consider the following statements:
S1 : A model with high variance is likely to overfit the training data.
S2 : A model with high bias is likely to underfit the data.
Which following is correct?
questions.solution:
(c)
• High variance means the model learns the noise in training data, resulting in overfitting and poor generalization. So, S1 is correct.
• High bias means the model is too simple to learn patterns, leading to underfitting. So, S2 is correct.

options.html: Cross-validation helps select the best parameters in LDA to avoid overfitting.
LDA does not require cross-validation because it always generalizes well.
Cross-validation splits data into training and testing sets to evaluate LDA’s performance.
Cross-validation is only useful for unsupervised learning methods.

questions.solution:
(a, c)
• Cross-validation is commonly used with LDA to tune parameters (like regularization) and prevent overfitting. So, option (a) is correct.
• LDA can overfit, especially with high-dimensional data, so cross-validation is useful. So, option (b) is incorrect.
• Cross-validation involves splitting data into training and testing sets to evaluate model performance reliably. So, option (c) is correct.
• Cross-validation is widely used for both supervised (like LDA) and unsupervised methods. So, option (d) is incorrect.

Which of the following is true regarding the effect of k in k-fold cross-validation?

options.html: Increasing k increases the bias of the error estimate.
Increasing k increases the variance of the error estimate.
Increasing k decreases the size of the training set in each fold.

questions.solution:
(b)
• Bias decreases with higher k, because the model gets trained on more data. So, option (a) is incorrect.
• Variance increases, since small changes in training data (especially in LOOCV) lead to large changes in validation error. So, option (b) is correct.
• Computational cost increases with more folds (more training runs). So, option (c) is incorrect.
• Training set size actually increases with higher k, not decreases. So, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.html: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.html: Soft Margin SVM is preferred when data contains noise or outliers.
Hard Margin SVM is preferred when data is noisy.
Soft Margin SVM is unsuitable for overlapping classes.
Hard Margin SVM works well with non-linearly separable data.

questions.solution:
(a)
• Soft Margin SVM uses slack variables to allow some misclassification or margin violations,
making it suitable for noisy data or data with outliers. So, option (a) is correct.
• Hard Margin SVM requires perfect linear separability and does not tolerate noise or
misclassification, so it is not preferred for noisy data. So, option (b) is incorrect.
• Soft Margin SVM is designed to handle overlapping classes by allowing margin violations via
slack variables. So, option (c) is incorrect.
• Hard Margin SVM cannot handle non-linearly separable data because it requires a strict linear
separation without any errors. So, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.html: Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.html: LDA can reduce dimensionality while preserving class separability.
LDA works best when class distributions are Gaussian.
LDA ignores class labels during computation.
LDA requires more data points than features to work properly.

questions.solution:
(a, b)
• LDA reduces dimensionality by projecting data onto directions that maximize class separability.
So, option (a) is correct.
• LDA assumes classes have Gaussian distributions with equal covariance matrices. So, option (b) is correct.
• LDA is supervised and uses class labels to find the best projection. So, option (c) is incorrect.
• Although having more data points than features is generally good for statistical methods, it is
not a strict requirement of LDA itself. So, option (d) is incorrect.

questions.html:
Consider the following statements:
S1 : Decision Trees are prone to overfitting, especially when they are allowed to grow deep without pruning.
S2 : Cross-Validation provides an unbiased estimate of model performance by using multiple training and validation splits.
Which of the above is true?
questions.solution:
(c)
• Decision Trees can overfit the training data if they grow too deep without pruning. So, S1 is true.
• Cross-Validation provides an unbiased performance estimate by using splits of the data for training and validation. So, S2 is true.

Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding decision tree handling of data?

options.html: Decision trees can directly work with both categorical features and continuous numeric features without preprocessing.
Decision trees require all features to be scaled before training.
Handling missing attribute values is not possible in decision trees.
Decision trees can naturally handle non-linear relationships between features and output.

questions.solution:
(a, d)
• Decision trees can handle categorical data by splitting based on categories directly, and numeric data by choosing threshold values to split. No mandatory feature scaling or transformation is needed. So, option (a) is correct.
• Decision trees do not require feature scaling because splits are based on thresholds or categories, not distance measures. So, option (b) is incorrect.
• Decision trees can handle missing values using various strategies such as surrogate splits,
treating missing as a separate category, or imputing values during training. So, option (c) is incorrect.
• Decision trees can model non-linear decision boundaries by hierarchical splits, making them
flexible for non-linear relationships. So, option (d) is correct.
